sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: UPPER AIR PATTERN WILL REMAIN DOMINATED BY STG ANTICYCLONIC GYRE ANCHORED OVER SRN PLAINS...WITH RIDGING EXTENDING NEWD ACROSS ONT. SHORTWAVE TROUGH -- EVIDENT IN MOISTURE CHANNEL IMAGERY OVER CENTRAL ONT AND N OF LH -- IS FCST TO AMPLIFY THROUGH PERIOD AS IT MOVES SEWD OVER NY AND NEW ENGLAND. THIS FEATURE WILL EVOLVE INTO BROAD MID-UPPER CYCLONE DURING 27/00Z-27/12Z TIME FRAME. ASSOCIATED SFC COLD FRONT -- INITIALLY ANALYZED FROM SWRN QUE SWWD ACROSS IL -- IS FCST TO MOVE SEWD TO NY...WRN PA...SRN OH AND NRN KY DURING 27/00Z-27/06Z TIME FRAME. FARTHER W...SUBTLE SHORTWAVE TROUGH -- NOW EVIDENT IN PROFILER/VWP DATA OVER PORTIONS CENTRAL CO -- IS EXPECTED TO LIFT SLOWLY NEWD ACROSS CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS EARLY IN PERIOD. PERTURBATION THEN WILL MOVE ACROSS NRN NEB/SRN SD REGION BETWEEN ABOUT 26/18Z-26/21Z...THEN ENEWD SRN MN/WI AND DEAMPLIFYING THROUGH EVENING/OVERNIGHT HOURS. SFC COLD FRONT -- NOW OVER MT -- IS EXPECTED TO MOVE EWD AND SEWD ACROSS DAKOTAS AND CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS...WITH WEAK FRONTAL-WAVE LOWS POSSIBLE LATE AFTERNOON INVOF ND/SD BORDER AND CENTRAL NEB. WARM FRONT SHOULD LIFT NWD ACROSS CENTRAL/NRN NEB INTO S-CENTRAL SD. MEANWHILE...FORMERLY CUT-OFF UPPER LOW -- INITIALL

sections.title: CENTRAL/NRN PLAINS
sections.text: SEVERAL AREAS OF SVR TSTMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP BETWEEN ND AND CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS -- PRIMARILY DURING AFTERNOON. CONDITIONAL THREAT ALSO EXISTS FOR TORNADIC SUPERCELLS OVER PORTIONS SRN SD AND NRN NEB...INVOF SFC FRONTAL ZONE. MODIFIED ETA-KF AND NAM FCST SOUNDINGS SUGGEST SMALL AREA WHERE VERY LARGE HODOGRAPHS WITH 0-1 KM SRH LOCALLY EXCEEDING 400 J/KG...EFFECTIVE SHEAR MAGNITUDES 45-55 KT...MLCAPE AOA 2000 J/KG...AND MID 60S-LOW 70S F SFC DEW POINTS SUPPORTING LOW LCL...ALL BECOME JUXTAPOSED. POTENTIAL COMPLICATING FACTORS...HOWEVER...INCLUDE INDICATIONS OF THICK MID-UPPER CLOUD COVER...AS WELL AS UNCERTAINTIES REGARDING CONVECTIVE MODES OF POTENTIAL TSTMS MOVING NEWD FROM WEAKER SHEARED AREAS S OF FRONT. POTENTIAL MAY DEVELOP FOR ONE OR TWO SIGNIFICANT TORNADO PRODUCING SUPERCELLS...BUT IT IS TOO SOON TO CONCENTRATE ANY SUCH PROBABILITIES ATTM GIVEN MESOSCALE UNCERTAINTIES. OTHERWISE...DAMAGING GUSTS AND LARGE HAIL ARE LIKELY FROM CONVECTION ALONG/AHEAD OF COLD FRONT...INCLUDING BOTH SUPERCELLS AND COMPLEX/FORWARD-PROPAGATING CLUSTERS. TWO OR THREE CLUSTERS MAY PERSIST AFTER NIGHTFALL ACROSS PORTIONS NEB...DAKOTAS AND MN WITH CONTINUED POTENTIAL FOR SVR WIND AND HAIL...AND P

sections.title: NERN CONUS TO CENTRAL APPALACHIAN REGION
sections.text: SCATTERED TSTMS IN BANDS AND CLUSTERS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP ALONG AND ESPECIALLY AHEAD OF SFC FRONTAL ZONE...INVOF PREFRONTAL TROUGHS AS WELL AS OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES LEFT BY PRIOR CONVECTION. MAIN THREAT SHOULD BE DAMAGING GUSTS FROM FORWARD-PROPAGATING CONVECTIVE COMPLEXES OF VARYING SIZES AND SHAPES. ACTIVITY SHOULD MOVE GENERALLY EWD FROM NRN MID-ATLANTIC TO NEW ENGLAND AND SEWD TO SWWD ACROSS CENTRAL APPALACHIANS REGION...LATTER BEING BENEATH STG NLY COMPONENT OF MID-UPPER FLOW BEHIND TROUGH. WITHIN BROAD OUTLOOK CORRIDOR...ONE OR TWO RELATIVELY DENSE/CONCENTRATED AREAS OF SVR WIND ARE LIKELY...FOCUSED NEAR MESOBETA SCALE BOUNDARIES AND POCKETS OF STG/SUSTAINED HEATING. ATTM...HOWEVER...IT IS TOO SOON TO DELINEATE SUCH CORRIDORS. AREAS OF MLCAPE 1500-2500 J/KG -- SUPPORTED BY SFC DEW POINTS MID 60S TO LOW 70S AND JUXTAPOSED WITH FAVORABLE SHEAR FOR SUPERCELLS -- ALSO INDICATE LARGE HAIL IS LIKELY OVER PORTIONS MID-ATLANTIC AND PERHAPS NEW ENGLAND. CONDITIONAL TORNADO POTENTIAL ALSO EXISTS OVER SERN NY/NERN NJ ACROSS PORTIONS SRN/SWRN NEW ENGLAND...WHERE SUFFICIENT VEERING/STRENGTHENING OF FLOW WITH HEIGHT AND SOMEWHAT ENLARGED LOW LEVEL HODOGRAPHS ARE EVIDENT IN PROGS. KINEMATI

sections.title: INTER-MOUNTAIN W AND GREAT BASIN
sections.text: WIDELY SCATTERED TSTMS SHOULD DEVELOP OVER PORTIONS OF THIS REGION DURING AFTERNOON HOURS. HIGHER TERRAIN WILL BE STRONGLY DIABATICALLY HEATED BENEATH AREA OF WEAK LARGE-SCALE ASCENT SPREADING AHEAD OF EJECTING CA/NV TROUGH. DEEP-LAYER SHEAR PROFILES MAY FAVOR ONE OR TWO ORGANIZED CLUSTERS OR BANDS OF HIGH-BASED TSTMS PRODUCING STG-SVR GUSTS OVER LOWER ELEVATIONS/BASINS. ..EDWARDS/GARNER.. 06/26/2009

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A DEVELOPING CLOSED LOW WILL DIG SEWD OVER NEW ENGLAND WHILE AN UPSTREAM SHORTWAVE TROUGH PROGRESSES EWD FROM THE INTERIOR PAC NW TO THE NRN HIGH PLAINS. FARTHER S...A PRONOUNCED MID-UPPER HIGH WILL REMAIN ANCHORED OVER THE SRN PLAINS. A SURFACE COLD FRONT ASSOCIATED WITH THE NEW ENGLAND MID LEVEL LOW WILL MOVE SEWD ACROSS NY/PA AND THE OH VALLEY THROUGH THIS EVENING. THIS BOUNDARY WILL THEN EXTEND NWWD FROM THE CONFLUENCE OF THE MS/OH RIVERS TO A LEE CYCLONE IN THE DAKOTAS. THE LEE CYCLONE IS EXPECTED TO DEVELOP NEWD FROM NW SD ACROSS ND THROUGH LATE TONIGHT...AS A COLD FRONT MOVES EWD/SEWD ACROSS THE NRN AND CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS IN ASSOCIATION WITH THE NRN ROCKIES MID LEVEL TROUGH. THE THREAT FOR STRONG/SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WILL BE FOCUSED ALONG THE SURFACE FRONTS...GENERALLY DOWNSTREAM FROM THE NEW ENGLAND AND NRN ROCKIES MID LEVEL TROUGHS.

sections.title: CENTRAL APPALACHIANS TO NEW ENGLAND TODAY
sections.text: IN THE WAKE OF WEAKENING MORNING STORMS OVER KY/TN...LOW-LEVEL RECOVERY FROM THE W/NW WILL SUPPORT STRONG INSTABILITY THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS THE MID MS AND OH VALLEYS ALONG THE COLD FRONT...WHERE AFTERNOON TEMPERATURES IN THE 90S WILL COINCIDE WITH BOUNDARY LAYER DEW POINTS IN THE LOW-MID 70S. FARTHER NE FROM THE CENTRAL APPALACHIANS INTO SRN NEW ENGLAND...MORE MODEST INSTABILITY IS ANTICIPATED WITH AFTERNOON TEMPERATURES IN THE UPPER 70S TO LOW 80S AND DEW POINTS IN THE MID-UPPER 60S. THE STRONGER MID LEVEL FLOW AND RESULTANT DEEP LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR IS EXPECTED TO BE CENTERED OVER PA...WITH GRADUAL WEAKENING OF THE VERTICAL SHEAR BOTH TO THE NE IN CLOSER PROXIMITY TO THE MID LEVEL LOW...AND TO THE SW CLOSER TO THE SRN PLAINS MID LEVEL RIDGE. THE NET RESULT WILL BE A RATHER LONG CORRIDOR WITH SOME POTENTIAL FOR ORGANIZED MULTICELL CLUSTERS DRIVEN MORE BY MLCAPE AOA 3000 J/KG TOWARD THE LOWER OH VALLEY AND SOMEWHAT STRONGER BULK SHEAR OVER PA/SRN NEW ENGLAND. DAMAGING DOWNBURST WINDS WILL BE THE PRIMARY SEVERE THREAT...THOUGH ISOLATED LARGE HAIL WILL ALSO OCCUR WITH THE STRONGEST STORMS.

sections.title: CENTRAL AND NRN PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT
sections.text: A SWATH OF MID 60S TO LOWER 70S BOUNDARY LAYER DEW POINTS REMAINS FROM CENTRAL MO NWWD INTO CENTRAL SD...WITH A COLD POOL EVIDENT ACROSS CENTRAL/ERN NEB AS OVERNIGHT CONVECTION SLOWLY WEAKENS IN SE NEB. SOME FORM OF THIS COLD POOL/OUTFLOW BOUNDARY MAY PERSIST TODAY WHILE RETREATING SLOWLY NWD ACROSS NEB...AND THE LEE TROUGH/COLD FRONT WILL GRADUALLY CONSOLIDATE ACROSS THE NRN HIGH PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING. THESE SURFACE BOUNDARIES...ALONG WITH WEAK SPEED MAXIMA EJECTING NEWD IN ADVANCE OF THE NRN ROCKIES TROUGH...WILL HELP FOCUS THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON FROM CENTRAL/WRN NEB NWD INTO SD/ND NEAR THE SURFACE LOW. LOW-MID LEVEL GRADIENT FLOW WILL GRADUALLY INCREASE THROUGH THE AFTERNOON OVER THE NRN PLAINS...WITH A 30 KT SLY LLJ EXPECTED BENEATH A BELT OF 30-40 KT SWLY MID LEVEL FLOW FROM WRN/CENTRAL NEB INTO SRN/CENTRAL SD. THIS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO SUFFICIENT DEEP LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR FOR SUPERCELLS. THE INITIAL STORMS WILL BE CAPABLE OF PRODUCING LARGE HAIL AND A FEW TORNADOES...GIVEN THE RELATIVELY MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER AND INCREASING LOW-LEVEL SHEAR DURING THE AFTERNOON/EVENING...ESPECIALLY ALONG AND N OF THE LINGERING OUTFLOW BOUNDARY IN NEB. LATER IN THE EVENING

sections.title: UT/WRN CO NWD INTO THE NRN ROCKIES
sections.text: THE REMNANTS OF THE PREVIOUSLY CLOSED LOW OVER SRN CA WILL EJECT NEWD TODAY OVER THE GREAT BASIN. ENTRAINMENT OF A MONSOONAL MOISTURE PLUME FROM MEXICO...ASCENT DOWNSTREAM FROM THE EJECTING WAVE...AND DAYTIME HEATING IN CLOUD BREAKS WILL SUPPORT SCATTERED THUNDERSTORM FORMATION FROM LATE MORNING INTO THE AFTERNOON. WEAK TO MODERATE INSTABILITY IN CONJUNCTION WITH STRENGTHENING MID-UPPER FLOW WILL SUPPORT ORGANIZED MULTICELL CLUSTERS/LINE SEGMENTS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING ISOLATED DAMAGING OUTFLOW WINDS AND MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL THROUGH THIS AFTERNOON. ..THOMPSON/SMITH.. 06/26/2009

sections.title: NORTHEAST
sections.text: CYCLONIC FLOW ALOFT AND RELATIVELY COOL MID LEVEL TEMPERATURES ARE IN PLACE THIS MORNING OVER MUCH OF THE NORTHEAST UNITED STATES. SCATTERED MORNING SHOWERS AND THUNDERSTORMS ARE ONGOING OVER NY/VT/CT...AND OVER PARTS OF ONTARIO/QUEBEC AND WESTERN ME. POCKETS OF CLOUD COVER AND PRECIPITATION THROUGHOUT THE REGION WILL COMPLICATE THE FORECAST OF WHERE/WHEN STRONG CONVECTION MAY DEVELOP THIS AFTERNOON. HOWEVER...A COMBINATION OF SUFFICIENT DEEP LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR AND MODERATE CAPE VALUES WILL POSE A RISK OF ORGANIZED MULTICELL THUNDERSTORMS CAPABLE OF LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL FROM ME INTO PA/NJ.

sections.title: OH VALLEY AND MID ATLANTIC
sections.text: STRONG DAYTIME HEATING HAS BEGUN ACROSS MUCH OF THE OH VALLEY AND CENTRAL APPALACHIANS...INTO VA/MD. TEMPERATURES WILL CLIMB INTO THE 80S/90S OVER THIS REGION WITH DEWPOINTS IN THE UPPER 60S TO LOWER 70S. THIS WILL YIELD A CORRIDOR OF STRONG INSTABILITY FROM MO/AR EASTWARD. SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP ALONG/AHEAD OF THE WEAK COLD FRONT MOVING SOUTHWARD ACROSS THE OH VALLEY THIS AFTERNOON. THE BEST COMBINATION OF CAPE/SHEAR WILL BE OVER PARTS OF WV/EASTERN KY...BUT SUFFICIENT PARAMETERS SUGGEST A RISK OF SEVERE STORMS THROUGHOUT THE AREA. WARM TEMPERATURES ALOFT MAY MITIGATE THE RISK OF LARGE HAIL...BUT LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE IN STRONGER CELLS.

sections.title: NORTHERN/CENTRAL PLAINS
sections.text: SATELLITE LOOPS SHOW A SHORTWAVE TROUGH LIFTING NORTHEASTWARD ACROSS UT/CO. THIS FEATURE IS EXPECTED TO SPREAD INTO THE NORTHERN PLAINS BY THIS EVENING. STRONG HEATING IS OCCURRING OVER MOST OF THE DAKOTAS AND NORTHERN NEB...WHERE AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES ARE EXPECTED TO REACH 3000-4000 J/KG. MODEL GUIDANCE IS IN GOOD AGREEMENT THAT THUNDERSTORMS WILL INTENSIFY BY MID/LATE AFTERNOON FROM THE BLACK HILLS SOUTHWARD INTO WESTERN NEB...AND EVENTUALLY NORTHWARD INTO THE CENTRAL DAKOTAS. THESE STORMS MAY INITIALLY BE SUPERCELLULAR WITH A RISK OF A FEW TORNADOES. STORMS ARE LIKELY TO ORGANIZE INTO A LINEAR MCS AND TRACK EASTWARD ACROSS THE DAKOTAS AND NEB THROUGH THE EVENING WITH A CONTINUED RISK OF LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. MESOSCALE MODELS SUGGEST SOME RISK OF BOW ECHO FORMATION OVER THIS REGION...SUGGESTING A MORE CONCENTRATED RISK OF DAMAGING WINDS IF THIS OCCURS.

sections.title: GREAT BASIN
sections.text: A RATHER COOL UPPER TROUGH CONTINUES TO DIG SOUTHWARD ACROSS CA/NV THIS MORNING. STEEP MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND POCKETS OF HEATING WILL RESULT IN SUFFICIENT INSTABILITY FOR SCATTERED AFTERNOON THUNDERSTORMS AHEAD OF THE TROUGH ACROSS MUCH OF THE GREAT BASIN. FORECAST SOUNDINGS SHOW MLCAPE VALUES OF 500-1000 J/KG AND EFFECTIVE SHEAR OF 25-35 KNOTS. THIS SHOULD BE SUFFICIENT FOR A FEW ORGANIZED MULTICELL OR ISOLATED HIGH-BASED SUPERCELL STORMS CAPABLE OF HAIL AND GUSTY/DAMAGING WINDS. AREAL COVERAGE OF SEVERE ACTIVITY REMAINS IN QUESTION...SO WILL MAINTAIN ONLY LOW PROBABILITIES OF SEVERE WEATHER AT THIS TIME.

sections.title: CENTRAL GULF COAST
sections.text: MORNING RAOBS FROM LA/MS/AL SHOW AMPLE MOISTURE/INSTABILITY FOR SCATTERED AFTERNOON AND EVENING THUNDERSTORMS...ALONG WITH SUBSTANTIAL DRY AIR ALOFT/DCAPE. THIS MAY HELP TO ENHANCE CONVECTIVE DOWNDRAFTS AND CONTRIBUTE TO A RISK OF ISOLATED WET MICROBURSTS IN STRONGER CORES. ..HART/HURLBUT.. 06/26/2009

THIS OUTLOOK WILL MAINTAIN LOW SEVERE WIND/HAIL PROBABILITIES FOR THIS REGION.
